summary.text: Mike Steele is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 12-Position 2, in office since January 9, 2017, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Maggie Adams.
He is also executive director of the Lake Chelan Chamber of Commerce and ranking member of the House Capital Budget Committee.

paragraphs.text: Steele is a lifelong resident of the Lake Chelan Valley and a graduate of Manson High School, and he earned degrees in business administration and political science at Pacific Lutheran University.

He then served in the White House Office of Political Affairs for the Northwestern United States under President George W. Bush and later worked for the House Republican Caucus leadership during the 2006 legislative session and interim.
He became executive director of the Lake Chelan Chamber of Commerce, a role his biography says he has held for more than 20 years.

Steele is a former member of the Chelan City Council and a past president of the Lake Chelan Rotary Club, and he is active in the Lake Chelan Community Hospital Foundation and serves as a trustee of the Association of Washington Business and the North Central Washington Community Foundation.
He was sworn into the House in 2017, and his biography lists his priorities as economic vitality, sustainable job growth and career and technical education.
It says he is ranking member of the Capital Budget Committee and sits on the Education and Consumer Protection and Business committees.
